tips.title: Wave before hello
tips.text: Get their eyes first, then sign hello. Wave where they can see you, or tap a shoulder.

tips.title: Keep thank you in view
tips.text: Sign thank you from chest to chin, in front of you. Thank you in your lap is hard to see.

tips.title: Lower brows on how are you
tips.text: How are you is not a yes or no. Lower your eyebrows on how are you and hold them down to the end.

tips.title: Sign slow more clearly
tips.text: When you sign slow, make the shape fully, then add speed. Rushed slow is hard to read.

tips.title: Ask for sign slow
tips.text: If you miss a sign, sign slow or again. Sign slow is a normal part of learning.

tips.title: Nod with yes
tips.text: When you sign yes, nod your head while the fist nods. If your head stays still, yes looks unfinished.

tips.title: Shake your head with no
tips.text: When you sign no, shake your head while the fingers flick. Do both at the same time.

tips.title: Raise your brows on really
tips.text: Really is a yes or no. Raise your eyebrows on really and keep them up until you finish.

tips.title: Wait until they finish
tips.text: Wait means let one person finish first. Start your sign after a clear pause.

tips.title: Sign have a good day
tips.text: Have a good day is one motion. Do not sign have, then good, then day.

tips.title: Use one point for I
tips.text: I is a point at yourself. English uses extra words. That one point can mean I.

tips.title: I and me are the same
tips.text: I and me are the same sign: point at yourself.

tips.title: Use a flat hand for his
tips.text: His and her face a flat palm toward them. That is not the same as pointing for he or she.

tips.title: Point back for he
tips.text: When you set a person to one side, point back to that same spot for he. That point means them again.

tips.title: Point for he and she
tips.text: He, she, him, and her are the same point at that person. Do not use a flat palm.

tips.title: Point or use a flat palm
tips.text: A point at someone is he. A flat palm toward them is yours. A flat palm on your chest is mine.

tips.title: Lower your brows on who
tips.text: Who is not a yes or no. Lower your eyebrows on who. Do the same for what, where, and why.

tips.title: Smile with happy
tips.text: When you sign happy, smile. A blank face makes happy look unfinished.

tips.title: Skip English on your lips
tips.text: When you sign sign language, skip English on your lips. Let your hands carry sign language.

tips.title: Don't invent a name sign
tips.text: Name sign is given by a Deaf person. Until then, fingerspell your name. Do not invent a name sign.

tips.title: Look at the person
tips.text: Look at the Deaf person you are talking with, not at the interpreter.

tips.title: Fingerspell at a calm pace
tips.text: When you fingerspell a name, hold a steady beat. Rushing makes letters blur together.

tips.title: Relax your spelling hand
tips.text: When you fingerspell a name, keep the hand easy, not clenched. Tight fingers hide letters.

tips.title: Bounce double letters
tips.text: When you fingerspell a name with a double letter, bounce the hand once. Do not hold the letter twice.

tips.title: Fingerspell by your shoulder
tips.text: When you fingerspell a name, keep the hand up by your shoulder, in a small space. Do not spell in your lap.

tips.title: Fingerspell names
tips.text: When you fingerspell a name, spell it letter by letter. Everyday words still use a regular sign.

tips.title: Use both hands for help
tips.text: Help uses two hands. The lower hand stays still. The top hand moves onto it.

tips.title: Move give toward them
tips.text: When you sign give, the hand moves toward the other person, not back toward you. Tell works the same way.

tips.title: Sign today first
tips.text: Put today at the start, then the rest of the sentence. Tomorrow works the same way.

tips.title: Watch the face
tips.text: When you sign face, look at the eyebrows and mouth, not only the hands. The face is part of the sign.

tips.title: Keep watching the face
tips.text: Stay on the face while they sign. A small nod shows you are following.
